fact: The Ministry of Public Health's own plan calls it the ministry's DHIS2 and the national health information system, adopted in 2017 as the integrated platform replacing fragmented donor-supported sub-systems; no date is given for the ownership statement, so the published date is used.

The PSNSN 2026-2030 names DHIS2 in costed activity 5.4.1 (strengthening its management plan and its interoperability framework) and in its 2026 budget lines, and states that a Strategic Plan for the National Health Information System 2026-2030 was in final validation; dated to the plan's publication.

The ministry states that DHIS2 was among the projects financed through partner conventions (WHO, GIZ, CDC, CHAI, PEPFAR, Global Fund) under the 2020-2024 plan, that funds obtained were about 0.5% of that plan's budget, and that there was no dedicated national digital health budget and strong dependence on external partners.

The ministry gives completeness of Monthly Activity Reports in DHIS2 as rising from 11.4% in 2017 to 80.1% in 2020, with aggregate data available by district and region, but gives no count or share of facilities entering their own reports.

The ministry published the PSNSN 2026-2030 in March 2026 with 2026 budget lines for DHIS2 deployment, maintenance, servers and interoperability, and reported a 2026-2030 national health information system plan aiming at complete digitalisation in final validation.
The ministry states that the electronic medical record (DME, on Bahmni) was deployed in about fifty pilot health facilities during the 2020-2024 plan, without saying how many are primary clinics.
The ministry lists the electronic medical record (Bahmni) among applications implemented or deployed by MINSANTE and its partners under the 2020-2024 plan.
The ministry names the electronic medical record among projects that drew on partner financing under the 2020-2024 plan, in a period with no dedicated national digital health budget.

The PSNSN 2026-2030 budgets, under objective 5.2 (hospital management applications in 50% of facilities by 2030), the selection of a partner and a public-private partnership contract to implement and deploy an electronic medical record in health facilities; dated to the plan's publication.

The plan published in March 2026 schedules in 2026 the selection of a partner and signature of a PPP contract for a national electronic medical record; it also records that facility heads have prioritised financial management software over clinical records.

EUDiF states that SmartMobileClinic, with which rural health workers create and track digital healthcare records, was launched in 2022 and is run by the German association Mapubi e.V. with the Health and Research Organisation Cameroon, the Ministry of Health being a stakeholder invited to review calls.
The SmartMobileClinic expansion is an 18-month action (September 2025 to February 2027) of the EU Global Diaspora Facility, with no domestic funding stated.

EUDiF states the project trains about 30 people from 12 target rural communities and runs 12 one- to two-day campaigns with local health facilities to bring the app into use in rural health centres; no count of facilities using it is given.

From September 2025 SmartMobileClinic is being extended to further rural communities, with a training of trainers in Yaoundé in December 2025 and 12 rural campaigns between November 2025 and January 2026.

The national statistics institute describes DHIS 2 as the national health information management system run by the Ministry of Public Health (MINSANTE); no date is attached to the statement, so the report's date of August 2023 is used.

The national statistics institute states that DHIS2 carries aggregate patient data from the Monthly Activity Reports of all health facilities across the national territory, and uses those reports for 2018 to 2022; it does not break the facilities down by level.
